prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
Liberal Democrats Manifesto 2024 – Summary (under 500 words)

Core vision: A “Fair Deal” built on five themes — a stronger, greener economy; high-quality public services; a clean, restored environment; a more international, cooperative UK; and a truly fair democracy.

Economy and jobs
- Responsible public finances; restore stability and growth through green investment, skills and innovation.
- Repair the relationship with Europe; remove trade barriers now (e.g., veterinary and plant agreements) and aim long-term to rejoin the Single Market.
- Industrial strategy focused on clean tech, digital and biosciences; gigabit broadband nationwide.
- Support SMEs: replace business rates with a Commercial Landowner Levy; expand the British Business Bank; tackle late payments.
- Fairer taxes: reverse bank tax cuts; a proper one-off windfall tax on oil and gas; raise Digital Services Tax to 6%; close CGT loopholes; 4% levy on FTSE-100 share buybacks.
- Skills: replace the apprenticeship levy with a flexible skills levy; £5,000 Lifelong Skills Grants (aiming for £10,000); boost apprenticeships and careers advice.

Climate and energy
- Net zero by 2045; 90% of electricity from renewables by 2030.
- Ten-year home energy upgrade: free insulation and heat pumps for low-income households; zero-carbon standard for all new buildings; social energy tariff; decouple electricity from gas prices.
- Rooftop solar push; more interconnectors and storage; no fracking or new coal; end fossil fuel subsidies with a just transition.

Health and care
- Right to see a GP within 7 days (24 hours urgently), with 8,000 more GPs; universal 24/7 booking; expanded pharmacy role.
- Guarantee urgent/emergency NHS dentistry; fix dental contract.
- Mental health: walk-in hubs for young people everywhere; regular check-ups at key life stages; a qualified mental health professional in every school.
- Cancer: 100% start treatment within 62 days; more radiotherapy, cancer nurses and research.
- Social care: free personal care (Scotland model); workforce plan, Royal College of Care Workers, £2/hour Carer’s Minimum Wage; paid carer’s leave and guaranteed respite.

Education and families
- Real-terms per-pupil funding rises; repair crumbling buildings; a “Tutoring Guarantee” for disadvantaged pupils.
- Early years: extra five free hours for disadvantaged 3–4 year olds; triple Early Years Pupil Premium; restore Erasmus+; reinstate maintenance grants.
- Extend free school meals to all children in poverty.
- Parental leave: double Statutory Maternity/Shared Parental Pay to £350/week; 90% pay for paternity; make all leave/pay day-one rights, including for self-employed.

Housing
- Build 380,000 homes a year (150,000 social); 10 new garden cities; empower councils on land value and Right to Buy.
- Renters: ban no-fault evictions; default three-year tenancies; national landlord register.
- Abolish leasehold; cap ground rents; expand Rent to Own; remove dangerous cladding (no leaseholder costs).
- End rough sleeping next Parliament; scrap the Vagrancy Act.

Environment and food
- End sewage scandal: turn water firms into public benefit companies; ban executive bonuses until discharges/leaks end; replace Ofwat; Sewage Tax; real-time discharge data.
- Double nature by 2050; plant 60m trees/year; Clean Air Act; protect 30% of land/sea by 2030; deposit return scheme; phase out non-recyclable single-use plastics within three years.
- National Food Strategy; +£1bn/year to Environmental Land Management; uphold high trade standards; strengthen the Groceries Code Adjudicator.

Transport
- Accelerate EV rollout: more chargers, card access, 5% VAT on public charging; restore 2030 zero-emission car/small van mandate; reintroduce plug-in grant.
- Freeze rail fares; simplify ticketing; electrify rail; deliver Northern Powerhouse Rail; empower bus franchising; maintain £2 bus cap while reviewing fares; more funding for local roads and potholes.

Crime and justice
- Restore community policing; guarantee police attendance for all burglaries.
- New Online Crime Agency; halve offence-to-sentencing times; public health approach to youth violence.

Immigration and asylum
- End the Hostile Environment; scrap the Illegal Migration Act and Rwanda scheme; expand safe and legal routes; 3‑month standard for asylum decisions; allow work after 3 months; fair family visa rules.

Rights, democracy, defence, international
- Defend the Human Rights Act; ban conversion practices; repeal anti-protest laws; misogyny as a hate crime.
- Political reform: PR (STV) for MPs and English councils; cap donations; votes at 16; written federal constitution; stronger local power.
- Defence: rebuild Army towards 100,000; increase defence spending towards 2.5% of GDP; maintain nuclear deterrent; procurement reform; better housing and support for service families.
- Foreign policy: champion international law; back Ukraine (including using frozen Russian assets); restore 0.7% aid; fix EU ties via a four-stage roadmap; press for a Gaza ceasefire and a two‑state solution.
